newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P says Australia budget will not trigger upgrade.
newsitem.headline: S&P says Australia budget will not trigger upgrade.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Wednesday the 1997/98 Australian budget would not in itself trigger an upgrading in the country's credit rating but the positive rating outlook remained.
"The first reading is that this budget will not in itself trigger an upgrade," Rick Shepherd, Director of Public Finance and Corporate Utility Ratings at S&P, told Reuters.
"But we are reaffirming the rating of Australia and the positive outlook," he said.

"We adopted the positive outlook after the 1996/97 budget put a fiscal tightening in train," said Shepherd. "In the mid-year review, however, the government had seemed to have gone backwards on some of that."
"We wanted to see the government deal with this slippage -- it hasn't for 1997/98 but has in the out-years," he said.
"Now we have to wait and see there is not another deterioration in the budget position like there was in the last mid-year review," said Shepherd.
He said the agency would be carrying out a full review of Australia's credit position later this year.
"We'll have a clearer picture after that (review) on the timing of the upgrade," added Shepherd.
The government's 1997/98 (July-June) budget forecast an underlying budget deficit of A$3.9 billion and a headline surplus of A$6.4 billion, thanks largely to receipts from asset sales.
It also predicted underlying surpluses of A$1.6 billion in 1998/99, A$5.4 billion in 1999/00 and A$10.4 billion the year after that.
S&P presently rates Australia at AA.
